items.value: Only two of the four — Hedge Funds and Venture Capital — are Alternative Investment Funds
items.reasoning: Under the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012 an AIF is a privately pooled investment vehicle that is not covered by the mutual fund or collective investment scheme regulations. Venture capital funds fall in Category I and hedge funds in Category III, so both are AIFs. Bonds and stocks are conventional (traditional) instruments traded on regular markets and are precisely what 'alternative' investments are defined against, so neither counts. The tally is two.

items.value: Only buying/selling government bonds and buying/selling foreign currency are RBI income sources
items.reasoning: The RBI earns from interest on and trading in government securities (open market operations) and from returns on and dealings in foreign currency assets, so I and II are income. Pension fund management is the PFRDA's domain, not the RBI's. The RBI lends to banks and to the government under the LAF/MSF and ways-and-means route, never to private companies. Printing and distributing currency notes is an EXPENDITURE item in the RBI's accounts (the cost of security printing), not a source of income, which rules out option D.

items.value: Only two rows are correctly matched — the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and the Directorate General of Systems and Data Management
items.reasoning: Row I is wrong in its third column: the Directorate of Enforcement does enforce the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 (along with FEMA and PMLA), but it works under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, not the Internal Security Division-I of the Ministry of Home Affairs. Row II is correct — the DRI is the apex anti-smuggling agency enforcing the Customs Act, 1962, under CBIC in the Department of Revenue. Row III is correct — the Directorate General of Systems and Data Management sits under CBIC in the Department of Revenue and runs data analytics for tax administration. The judgement call is row III, whose analytics function overlaps with that of the DGARM.

items.value: Only the second statement is correct — BRSR disclosures are largely non-financial
items.reasoning: Statement I is wrong twice over: the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report is mandated by SEBI, not the Reserve Bank of India, and it applies to the top 1000 listed companies by market capitalisation, not to all listed companies. Statement II is correct — the BRSR is an ESG disclosure covering environmental, social and governance parameters, which are non-financial in character.

items.value: Statement I is wrong (poultry and wool rearing income is taxable); Statement II is correct (rural agricultural land is not a capital asset)
items.reasoning: Section 2(1A) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 defines agricultural income narrowly around rent/revenue from land, cultivation and allied processing; poultry farming, dairy farming and wool rearing fall outside it and are taxed as business income, so the exemption under Section 10(1) does not reach them and Statement I is not correct. Statement II is correct: Section 2(14) expressly excludes rural agricultural land from the definition of 'capital asset', which is why its sale attracts no capital gains tax.

items.value: Statements I and III are correct; India is not resource-rich in all 30 identified critical minerals
items.reasoning: India joined the Minerals Security Partnership in June 2023, so I is correct. III is correct: the MMDR Amendment Act, 2023 inserted Part D in the First Schedule listing critical and strategic minerals and empowered the Central Government to auction mining leases and composite licences for them exclusively. II is plainly false — the very reason India identified 30 critical minerals in 2023 was its heavy import dependence for lithium, cobalt, nickel and rare earths.

items.value: Both II and III are correct and both explain why bondholders face lower risk than stockholders
items.reasoning: All three statements are true. Statement II explains Statement I because a lender holds a contractual claim to fixed interest and principal, whereas an owner holds only a residual claim on whatever is left over. Statement III explains it too, and more directly: in liquidation and in the order of servicing, debt is paid before equity, so the stockholder absorbs losses first. Option B is wrong because it inverts the direction of explanation, and D is wrong because both II and III are correct.

items.value: Statements I and II are correct; the claim that no regulator warns investors or acts against unregistered advisors is false
items.reasoning: India does account for an overwhelming share of global equity option contracts traded by number, and its market capitalisation did overtake Hong Kong's in early 2024 to become the fourth largest in the world, so I and II hold. Statement III is false: SEBI is precisely that regulator — it has published studies on individual traders' losses in the F&O segment, issued repeated investor cautions, and taken enforcement action against unregistered investment advisors and finfluencers.

items.value: Both II and III are correct and both explain why a circular economy cuts greenhouse gas emissions
items.reasoning: All three statements are true of a circular economy. Statement II explains Statement I because extracting, transporting and processing virgin raw materials is highly energy- and emission-intensive, so substituting recovered material directly lowers emissions. Statement III also explains it, since less waste per unit of output means less energy and material consumed and less waste sent to landfill, where decomposition releases methane. Option B, which allows only one of the two to be explanatory, is the runner-up and the reason this is a judgement call rather than a certainty.

items.value: Statements I and II are correct; interest received on loans is a revenue receipt and creates no liability
items.reasoning: Statement I is the standard definition of a capital receipt — it either creates a liability or reduces an asset of the government. Statement II follows from it: borrowing creates a liability and disinvestment reduces the government's asset holding, so both are capital receipts. Statement III is wrong on both counts — interest RECEIVED is income to the government, is classified as a revenue receipt, and creates no liability whatsoever; it is interest PAID that reflects an existing liability.

items.value: Both statements about Raja Ram Mohan Roy are correct
items.reasoning: Roy was deeply learned in Sanskrit, Persian and Arabic, translated the Vedas and the Upanishads into Bengali and wrote extensively on Vedanta, so his respect for the traditional philosophical systems of the East is well attested — while he simultaneously held that modern culture was needed to regenerate Indian society. He equally championed rational and scientific enquiry, opposed superstition, and argued for human dignity and the social equality of men and women, most visibly through his campaign against sati and for women's rights to property and education.

items.value: Three of the four — boycott of law-courts and foreign cloth, strict non-violence, and panchayats for settling disputes
items.reasoning: The Non-Cooperation programme adopted at Calcutta and confirmed at Nagpur included boycott of British law-courts by lawyers and litigants and boycott of foreign cloth (I), and its constructive side included setting up panchayats to arbitrate disputes as a substitute for the boycotted courts (IV). Strict non-violence (II) was integral — Gandhi withdrew the entire movement after Chauri Chaura precisely because it was breached. Statement III inverts the programme: participants were to SURRENDER their titles and honorary offices, not retain them while refraining from public use. Hence three.

items.value: A large wheel with earthen pots tied to the outer ends of its spokes
items.reasoning: The name itself carries the answer: 'ara' means spoke and 'ghatta' means pot, so the araghatta is the spoked wheel fitted with pots that scoop water at the bottom of its rotation and empty it at the top — the ancestor of the Persian wheel. Option A describes the charas or mot, a leather bag drawn over a pulley by bullocks, which is a different device; options C and D describe simpler lift methods that involve no wheel at all.

items.value: Mahendravarman I, the Pallava ruler
items.reasoning: Mahendravarman I (c. 600–630 CE) is famous for the satirical Sanskrit farce Mattavilasa Prahasana, from which the title 'Mattavilasa' comes, and his inscriptions carry the epithets 'Vichitrachitta' (of curious mind) and 'Gunabhara', along with Chitrakarapuli and Chettakari. Simhavishnu was his grandfather, Narasimhavarman I his son and the conqueror of Vatapi (titled Mamalla), and Simhavarman belongs to the earlier Pallava line.

items.value: Chandragupta II
items.reasoning: Fa-hien travelled in India between roughly 399 and 414 CE, during the reign of Chandragupta II Vikramaditya, and his account Fo-kuo-ki describes a prosperous and lightly governed Madhyadesha. Samudragupta preceded him, while Kumaragupta I and Skandagupta ruled later — the Chinese pilgrim of Harsha's seventh-century court was Hiuen Tsang, not Fa-hien.

items.value: Rajendra I of the Chola dynasty
items.reasoning: Rajendra I launched the famous naval expedition of about 1025 CE across the Bay of Bengal against Srivijaya under its ruler Sangrama Vijayottungavarman, capturing Kadaram and other ports to secure the Chola trade route to China. The Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha, the Kakatiya Prataparudra and the Hoysala Vishnuvardhana were all inland powers of the Deccan with no comparable maritime campaign.

items.value: Only two pairs are correctly matched — Asmaka–Godavari and Kosala–Sarayu
items.reasoning: Asmaka (Assaka), the southernmost mahajanapada with its capital at Potana, lay on the Godavari, so I is right; and Kosala, with Ayodhya and Shravasti, lay on the Sarayu, so IV is right. Kamboja was a north-western janapada in the Hindukush region beyond the Indus, whereas the Vipas (Beas) flows through the Punjab plain, so II is mismatched. Avanti was centred on Ujjain on the Shipra and Mahishmati on the Narmada; the Mahanadi drains Chhattisgarh and Odisha, far to its east, so III is mismatched. Two correct.

items.value: Lahore
items.reasoning: Vishnu Digambar Paluskar founded the first Gandharva Mahavidyalaya at Lahore on 5 May 1901, opening formal Hindustani classical music training to the general public and freeing it from the closed gharana-household system. He later established a branch in Bombay in 1908; Gwalior and Ujjain are associated with his training and travels but not with the founding of the school.

items.value: District-level administration
items.reasoning: Ashoka's Third Rock Edict directs the Pradeshika, the Rajuka and the Yukta to go on tour (anusamyana) every five years to propagate dhamma and inspect administration, and these three are conventionally placed at the level between the province and the village. The Pradeshika headed a district, the Rajuka handled rural administration, land assessment and later judicial powers over the countryside, and the Yuktas were subordinate revenue and accounts officials attached to them. Provincial charge lay with the kumaras or viceroys, and the village had its gramika, which is why A, C and D are excluded.

items.value: Both statements about the Non-Cooperation Movement are correct
items.reasoning: At the Nagpur session of December 1920 the Congress amended its creed so that its objective became the attainment of Swaraj by all legitimate and peaceful means, which is Statement I. Statement II records the movement's staged design accurately: it opened with surrender of titles and boycott of courts, schools, councils and foreign cloth, and the harder measures of mass civil disobedience and non-payment of taxes were reserved for a later stage, to be taken up only if Swaraj had not been won within a year and the government had answered with repression.

items.value: Only four are NATO members — Bulgaria, Croatia, Sweden and North Macedonia
items.reasoning: Bulgaria joined NATO in 2004, Croatia in 2009, North Macedonia in 2020 and Sweden in March 2024, giving four. Austria is not a member — it is constitutionally neutral under its 1955 declaration and is only a Partnership for Peace participant. Serbia is likewise outside NATO, having declared military neutrality in 2007, and its relationship is limited to Partnership for Peace cooperation.

items.value: The Andes pass through four of them — Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela
items.reasoning: The Andes run the length of South America's western margin through seven countries: Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina. Of the six listed, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela are on that list — Venezuela through the Cordillera de Merida, the range's northern extension. Brazil lies east of the range and is dominated by the Amazon basin and the Brazilian Highlands, and landlocked Paraguay consists of the Gran Chaco and the Parana lowlands, so neither is crossed.

items.value: The equator passes through none of the three water bodies
items.reasoning: Lake Tanganyika lies wholly in the southern hemisphere, its northern tip reaching only about 3 degrees south, so the equator misses it — the East African lake the equator does cross is Lake Victoria. Tonle Sap is in Cambodia at roughly 13 degrees north, well inside the tropics but far from the equator, and the Patos Lagoon lies on the coast of Rio Grande do Sul in southern Brazil at about 30 to 31 degrees south. None of the three is intersected.

items.value: All three statements about Indian turmeric in 2022-23 are correct
items.reasoning: India is the world's largest producer, consumer and exporter of turmeric, accounting for the bulk of global output and trade, so I holds. More than thirty varieties of turmeric are cultivated across some twenty states, so II holds. Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are the leading producing states, as recorded in the material issued around the constitution of the National Turmeric Board, so III holds. The item turns on recalled production figures rather than on reasoning, which is why this is not marked HIGH.

items.value: All three are cited as evidence of continental drift
items.reasoning: All three are standard evidences advanced for Wegener's continental drift. The belt of ancient rocks of about 2,000 million years along the Brazilian coast matches a corresponding belt in western Africa, showing the two coasts were once joined. The placer gold deposits of the Ghana coast have no source rock in situ and are held to have been derived from the Brazilian plateau when the landmasses lay side by side. And the Gondwana sequence of sediments, with its tillite base recording ancient glaciation, is found with counterparts across six landmasses of the southern hemisphere.
